key_takeaway: Method change, not a market change: Server OEM earnings (Dell, Lenovo, HPE, Supermicro) now count as a leading indicator (A8, green), so the score reads 47.5 AMBER on the new 61-weight method; on the old method it is unchanged at 49.2 and nothing changed color. OEM orders and guides are rising (Dell AI servers +100% with a $95B backlog; Supermicro pre-announced Q1 well above guide). With the bigger denominator, no single flip reaches RED: E4 alone gives 49.2; E4 plus E5 gives 50.8.
pattern: Classic early stage of a capex bust: financing cracks while demand still looks intact. In telecom 2000–01, shale 2014–15 and crypto mining 2022, credit spreads on the most-levered builders and the unit price of capacity turned first; supplier volumes turned last. Today the levered edge (neoclouds, IPO candidates, Oracle) is under stress, but unit economics (GPU rents) and the supply chain (TSMC, server OEMs, ODMs, Korea exports) have not rolled. First monetization crack showing (C2 amber).
decisive: Financing window shut for good — lab/neocloud IPO pulled or GPU-backed loan default (T-15)
Hyperscaler cancelling capacity for demand reasons rather than grid (D2b), or Big-4 capex outrunning OCF while 2027 guides decelerate (T-16)
